groups.title: Videos
groups.lede: The films come first: a minute each, sound on, one idea per film. They are drawn frame by frame from real screenshots of the app, with Yui's own music, and the agent's words are scripted on the demo account. Below them, the short cuts, sound off, recorded in the iPhone simulator. Download any of them from the press kit at the bottom of this page.

entries.title: Yui 0.5.0: the crew feels ready
entries.what: The 0.5.0 release in two minutes: hold to snap and say what's in it, a meal without a scale, meet each agent and see what each one does, every agent's home and Gouda's looper, Yui handing you to Basil, and your tables moving to a Claude agent. Then the six agents that ship with Yui. Turn your sound on.

entries.title: Meet Yui, one evening
entries.what: One evening with Yui: talk and the words show as you say them, dinner as three recipes to tap and a timer on the lock screen, Saturday planned with one Send, Coach in its own look, then lessons, charts, games, music and timers. Your agents, on the whole screen.

entries.title: Meet Yui
entries.what: You asked for a timer and got an essay. In Yui, one line from your agent becomes the whole screen.

entries.title: Plan to launch
entries.what: One project start to finish: a pottery studio's website, from plan mode and picked photos to before and after, the reel and the timeline.

entries.title: Jam with your agent
entries.what: Music tools: a beat, your edits, a patch, chords on the circle of fifths, a solo.

entries.title: A lesson is one deck
entries.what: Compound interest as one deck: a diagram, the formula, a chart, a graded quiz and a calculator.

entries.title: Your agents, one app
entries.what: Every agent wears its own look. Add and pair one, @mention another, restyle Yui by asking.

entries.title: Built in public
entries.what: Feedback becomes a card, an agent builds it, it ships to TestFlight, and the site says so.

entries.title: The new face, filmed in the app
entries.what: Yui 0.4.1, filmed in the app: hold the big mic and talk, one question gets one screen back, longer answers play in parts, questions wait for one Send, the chat is the record, each agent moves its own way, and the picture behind the words listens. Turn your sound on.

entries.title: Yui lives on the full screen
entries.what: One question used to get eight pages. Now the stage answers: short parts with a picture each, questions last with one Send, and the chat is the record.

entries.title: Cook with your hands full
entries.what: Flour on your hands? Tap the mic once and just talk. Your agent walks you through dinner on the whole screen, and the oven timer keeps count on your lock screen.

entries.title: Can I afford it?
entries.what: Ask out loud about the car you want. Your agent answers with one number, then a calculator you drag, the whole cost side by side, and one Send.

entries.title: Homework rescue
entries.what: Stuck on fractions at 8 pm. Your agent shows it as a picture, turns it into a memory game and a quick check, then plans tomorrow from the score.

entries.title: History as a map that moves (concept)
entries.what: Ask for the rise and fall of the Mongol Empire and drag through 160 years: the empire grows across the steppe, splits into four khanates, carries silk and then the plague along the same roads, and becomes Friday's lesson with one Send. A concept film: not built yet.

entries.title: 2020, macro drawn (concept)
entries.what: A record high, then down a third in 33 days. One agent reads prices, the Fed and the jobs report, draws the whole machine, and six linked charts move under one finger. Historical data; education, not investment advice. A concept film: not built yet.

entries.title: On call at 3 am (concept)
entries.what: Checkout is failing at 3:07 am. One agent reads the alerts, logs, metrics and last night's deploys, finds the change, and asks before it rolls anything back. One Send, and back to sleep. A concept film: not built yet.

entries.title: Build to earn
entries.what: Use it, help build it, and it counts. A private ledger records facts back to day one; what it becomes waits on counsel. A proposal: no token exists, nothing is for sale.

entries.title: Agents chip in
entries.what: For agents: read the backlog, claim a card with a draft pull request titled with its key, run its tests. A person reviews every pull request; when it merges, the card closes.

entries.title: Lend your idle tokens
entries.what: Yui@home: paste one weekly prompt into your coding agent and your leftover tokens pick a card, do the work and open a pull request. A person reviews it; your keys stay yours.

entries.title: Presets, not code
entries.what: Why an agent sends one line instead of a page of Swift: 9 tokens against 25 and 75, it passes App Review, the taste lives in the app, and one line draws everywhere.

entries.title: A button, not a paragraph
entries.what: For agents: your human wants a button, not a wall of text. Send one line per control, hear every tap back, and reach their phone from Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code, your own model or a webhook.

entries.title: Yui in 15 seconds
entries.what: Ask your agent a question. It answers with a screen you can tap.

entries.title: Yui Lines in 30 seconds
entries.what: One line of Yui Lines becomes a screen. 1.6x fewer tokens than minified JSON.

entries.title: Your Hermes on your phone in 60 seconds
entries.what: Install the plugin, pair, and your own Hermes agent answers on your iPhone with a screen.

groups.title: Your own key
groups.lede: What is on main for the next build: when the free turns run out, bring your own key, from one sheet, at every stop. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator.

entries.title: The free turns run out, one card
entries.what: Use up your 100 free turns and Yui says so once, with one button: Add my key. It opens the key sheet. Nothing is cut off mid-thought and nothing asks for a card number.

entries.title: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok
entries.what: Pick a provider, paste a key, Save. Each has a default model that can read photos. The sheet says the plain thing: a Claude Pro or Max plan cannot pay for another app, only an API key can, and it links to where you make one. Or add Yui inside Claude or ChatGPT and your plan pays.

entries.title: The key sheet opens from every stop
entries.what: Settings, the limit card, Add agent and Controls, Model all open the same sheet, and so does the card a photo or lookup shows when it cannot run on free turns. OpenRouter is one tap to sign in, My computer needs no key, and a key can be set for one agent. It is kept locked away on Yui's server and the app never shows it again.

groups.title: Yui 0.6.2
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.6.2 (build 392, Sep 30): the first minute of a new user, fixed. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator.

entries.title: Open lands on the first question
entries.what: Tap Open on a crew card and the first question of the first plan is on screen, and it stays there. Before, it dropped back to a small chip after a second.

entries.title: Your week builds right after Send
entries.what: Answer the five questions, tap Send, and the week is built then. No second ask.

entries.title: The notifications ask comes once, after the plan
entries.what: After the first plan, one line asks if you want a nudge when your trainer checks in. It shows once and does not come back.

entries.title: Add an agent sits in the drawer
entries.what: Open the drawer and Add an agent is there, with one command to copy. Every screen has a menu button and a chat button, so the drawer is one tap away.

groups.title: Yui 0.6.0
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.6.0 (build 342, Sep 29): every one of the five has its own tools, flows and default screens now, not just chat, and a quiet visual behind all of them. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator.

entries.title: Coach's workout, week and progress
entries.what: Say Start today's workout and the session opens full screen, one move per page: tick each set, nudge the reps and the weight, say how it felt, then one Finish. Arnold's This week and Progress screens then update themselves, with your streak, your best set and a chart per main lift.

entries.title: Basil's meals, groceries and a swap
entries.what: Ask Basil to plan your meals and today's macros board comes up. Photograph a plate and he reads it. Add oat milk to my groceries ticks onto the list, and the list shares out of the phone. Ask for a swap and he swaps one meal, not the week.

entries.title: Gouda's songs, looper and practice
entries.what: Learn a song hands you the chord grid to play along. Make a beat opens the looper, Log practice keeps the session. His loop and his click keep playing while you move between his screens, and Tune up opens the tuner with no turn.

entries.title: Penny's week, today and the evening review
entries.what: Get your week out of your head out loud, then Plan my week draws it. What's next today? gives the today list, and Evening review closes the day. Reminders land on the phone's clock, and the order you saved holds.

entries.title: Quill teaches, quizzes and walks a problem
entries.what: Teach me something new opens a five minute lesson. Quiz me on what I learned scores the deck and sets the next review. Walk me through a math problem goes one step per page, and his Studying and Progress screens keep the score.

entries.title: Every agent opens on its own quiet visual
entries.what: From the first open each agent draws its own, behind what you came for: waves for Arnold, a bloom for Basil, grain for Gouda, an aurora for Penny, an orb for Quill. They are meant to be barely there. If one pulls your eye, that is a bug.

entries.title: Turn a visual off, and the phone can too
entries.what: Each agent's settings has a switch. Turn it off and its screen goes plain. Low Power or Reduce Motion drops every visual to one still frame on its own, so nothing moves when you have asked the phone for nothing to move.

entries.title: Hold the mic, slide to cancel or lock
entries.what: Hold the mic to talk. Slide left to throw the take away, or slide up onto the lock to keep recording with your thumb off the glass. Let go anywhere else and it sends.

entries.title: Every message says when it was sent
entries.what: Each message carries its time, and the thread breaks into days with a divider: Today, Yesterday, then the date. A long thread reads as a record instead of one run-on column.

entries.title: A notification opens on page one
entries.what: Tap a notification and the answer opens at its first page, not its last. You read what came in from the start, then swipe.

groups.title: The crew's tools
groups.lede: Yui 0.6.0 gives the crew real tools, and the agent side is live now: these answers reach the app you have today. Each tool is a flow with one Send, and its result lands on a screen that stays current.

entries.title: Start blank: make an agent in five taps
entries.what: Add agent ends with Start blank. A new empty agent asks one question at a time: its name, how it talks, its look, the screens it reaches for and its model, with Not sure and Skip on every step. One Make me, and it writes itself, greets you in the voice you picked and keeps it.

entries.title: Coach runs your workout
entries.what: Say Start today's workout and your session opens full screen, one move at a time: tick each set, nudge the reps and the weight (it starts from what you lifted last), say how it felt, then one Finish. Every set is logged.

entries.title: Coach's week, today and progress
entries.what: After Finish, Arnold's screens update by themselves: the day ticked on This week, today marked done, and Progress with your streak, your best set and a chart per main lift. Tap a day to change what it trains, or log a session you did away from the app.

entries.title: Coach's check-in, then the timer
entries.what: Sleep, anything sore, minutes free, your gear. Your answers pick the session (easy, a quick hit, bodyweight or strength), then one Send and the interval timer comes up with the moves, minus any that hit a spot that hurts. It runs in the site chat too: say show me a workout flow.
entries.yl: flow@session trainer-session

entries.title: Basil reads a plate, then your macros
entries.what: Pick a plate and Basil guesses the calories and macros and says how sure he is. When he is unsure he asks about the part he can't see, like the rice under a poke bowl. Fix the portion, pick the meal, one Save, and it lands in his meals with today's calories and macros against your goal. It runs in the site chat too: say show me how Basil logs a meal.
entries.yl: flow@plate nutritionist-plate

entries.title: Gouda turns a vibe into a beat
entries.what: Pick a vibe and Gouda builds the beat, kick and snare first, with its own tempo range. Change one row, pick the chords under it (moody asks for a minor key), one Keep, and the loop plays with the chords under it, kept in his sessions. It runs in the site chat too: say show me how Gouda makes a beat.
entries.yl: flow@jam musician-jam

entries.title: Penny turns a busy week into a plan
entries.what: Pick what's on this week and what matters most (a deadline asks when it's due), then when you get things done and how many a day. One Send and your week lands on a timeline by day with Edit order, plus a checklist to keep, what matters most at the top. It runs in the site chat too: say help me plan my busy week.
entries.yl: flow@busy planner-week

entries.title: Quill teaches a topic, then quizzes you
entries.what: Pick a topic (how vaccines work, how a ball flies or how money grows) and how much you know; the basics skip the first page. A short lesson, one idea and one picture a page, then one question: a miss gets a page on why. Say when to quiz you again, and a calculator comes up to play with, with three cards in your review. It runs in the site chat too: say teach me something and quiz me.
entries.yl: flow@study study-quiz

entries.title: Meet the crew, each with a flow to try
entries.what: Open the chat on yuigui.com and tap Meet the crew: the five starter agents on one screen, each in their own colors with one line on what they do. Tap one and the chat turns their color and plays their flow in their voice. After it, one like or dislike, then meet another.
entries.yl: choose@crew "Who do you want to meet?" Arnold|Basil|Gouda|Penny|Quill title="Meet the crew"

entries.title: Basil plans your week of meals
entries.what: Say Plan my meals and one full-screen flow asks how many days, meals a day, what you like, what to leave out, your budget and time to cook. One Send and your week lands as a deck, a page a day, where a tap on any meal swaps it.

entries.title: Basil's today, week and grocery list
entries.what: Basil's screens stay current by themselves: Today shows calories and macros against your goal, what's up next with I ate it, and each meal to fix. This week's meals has a swap button per meal, and the grocery list is grouped by aisle with ticks.

entries.title: Gouda teaches you a song
entries.what: Say Learn a song and one full-screen flow asks which song (or paste your own chords), what key and how fast to start. One Send puts the chords on big buttons with the click counting you in, ready to play along.

entries.title: Gouda's looper, chords, keys and practice
entries.what: Gouda's four screens stay current by themselves. Chords holds the song you're learning: tap Half to slow the click, tap a bar to loop it. Keys stays in the song's key, the Looper keeps the beats you saved, and Practice shows your streak and what to practice next.

entries.title: Log practice with Gouda
entries.what: Log practice asks how long, what you played and how it went, one Send. Or just say I practiced 20 minutes on scales, or play the click: it logs its own minutes when you stop it. Your streak and this week update on Practice.

entries.title: Penny plans your week by voice
entries.what: Say Plan my week and talk it out: everything on your plate, in any order. Then which days are full, how many things a day and whether to remind you, one Send. Penny sorts it into days and your week lands as a timeline you can drag around.

entries.title: Penny's today and this week
entries.what: Penny's two screens stay current by themselves. Today shows the next thing big with a Done button, the list with ticks and the evening review. This week is a timeline by day: Edit order to drag a task to another day, or pick a task and a day. A task with a time gets a reminder.

list@today title=Today "Renew the car registration"|"Pay the water bill"|"Groceries" +check

next "Call the dentist" at=Tomorrow sub="9:00 am"
next "Finish the report" at=Fri

entries.title: Penny's evening review
entries.what: Two minutes at the end of the day: what got done, then each task still open, done, tomorrow or drop, and how the day went. One Send and tomorrow starts clean.

entries.title: Quill teaches you a topic
entries.what: Say Teach me how vaccines work and one full-screen flow asks how much time you have and what you know already. One Send and a short lesson opens on the stage, one idea a page, ending in a quick quiz. What it taught becomes cards you review later.

entries.title: Quill's five minute lesson
entries.what: A real lesson from Quill: one idea a page with the key points, then a three question quiz that shows why when you miss one. Finish it and your score lands on Progress.

entries.title: Review your cards with Quill
entries.what: The cards due today in one flow: think of the answer, see it, then tap Again, Hard, Good or Easy. Again brings a card back today, Easy sends it furthest. One Send and every card knows when to come back.

entries.title: Quill's studying, next review and progress
entries.what: Quill's three screens stay current by themselves. What you're studying shows your decks, Next review the cards due today with a Start button, and Progress your streak, cards reviewed this week, cards learned and your last quiz.

stat@due 1 "Cards due today" sub="World capitals"
card@review-start "Review 1 card" "Think of the answer, then tap again, hard, good or easy." cta="Start review"
stat@streak 1 "Day streak" sub="Keep it going today"
chart@studied bar "Cards reviewed" x=Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun|Today y=0|0|0|0|0|0|8

entries.title: Quill walks you through a problem
entries.what: Say Walk me through a problem and type or say it. Quill breaks it into steps, one a page, each with a question. You answer each step before the next one shows, so you do the thinking.

groups.title: Yui 0.5.2
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.5.2 (build 288, Sep 28): the screen dots are back, and the screens slide with your finger instead of fading.

entries.title: Screen pills in the top bar
entries.what: Your screens sit in the top bar as pills, Home first, then each screen by name. Tap one to jump. Swipe between screens and the filled pill follows and scrolls into view. The row fades out at the right when it is long. No screens, no pills.

entries.title: The screen dots, in the bottom bar
entries.what: A small row of dots in the agent's colors sits in the bottom bar, centered between the page arrows and +, T and the mic, and slides over when the arrows show. Drag and the dot stretches and slides to the next one. Tap a dot to jump.

groups.title: Yui 0.5.0
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.5.0 (build 278): the crew feels ready. Hold to snap and say what's in it, meet each agent the first time you open it, every agent has a home with its own shortcuts and screens, and a meal gets logged without a scale. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: Hold to snap and say
entries.what: One press takes the photo. Keep holding and say what's in it: Two eggs in a lot of butter. Let go and the photo and your words go together.

entries.title: Log a meal without weighing
entries.what: Send Basil a photo and a few words. He answers at once, works out the macros behind the scenes, then posts one breakdown that fits a phone and remembers each food.

entries.title: Meet each agent
entries.what: Open an agent for the first time and its hello plays on the full screen. The picker at the top says what each one does, and About lists three things to ask it.

entries.title: Every agent has a home
entries.what: Its own shortcuts sit over the bar, like Start a workout. What waits on you is right there. Swipe left for its starter screens: Arnold's week, Gouda's looper.

entries.title: One agent opens another
entries.what: Ask Yui something that is Basil's job. Yui passes you over with a note, and Basil is already answering in his own thread.

entries.title: Switch agents, keep your tables
entries.what: Your tables belong to you, not to one agent. Hand Basil's Foods table to a Claude agent and the same question draws the same screen.

groups.title: Yui 0.4.1
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.4.1 (build 208, Sep 27): this one is for musicians. A tuner on the mic, a metronome in the chat, a Record button on every instrument, and a MIDI keyboard that plays the keys. Shots and clips are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: A tuner and a metronome
entries.what: Ask for a tuner and the app listens on the mic, lights the string you play and turns the needle green within 3 cents. Guitar, ukulele, bass or any note. Ask for a metronome and it clicks in the chat, in time with a playing beat, and tells the agent how long you practiced.
entries.yl: tuner ukulele

entries.title: Record a take, send it
entries.what: Record sits on the looper, the drum pads, the keys and the chords. It records what Yui plays, not the mic. Stop and send gives the agent the sound and the notes, like a photo you took.

entries.title: A MIDI keyboard plays the keys
entries.what: Plug in a USB keyboard or pair one over Bluetooth. It plays the keys on the screen, and each note lights up. While a beat plays, Yui sends MIDI clock, so a drum machine keeps time with it.

groups.title: Yui 0.4.0
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.4.0 (build 204, Sep 27): the new face of Yui. The answer plays on the full screen, a big mic sits bottom right, your agents top left, the stage moves the way each agent moves, and a live picture behind the words listens to your voice and the music. Keys, chords and real drums ride along. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: Yui lives on the full screen
entries.what: Ask something and the whole screen is the answer: a working line while the agent looks, then short parts, a line and a picture each, and the questions last with one Send. The chat is the record, behind the button top right.

entries.title: A big mic, bottom right
entries.what: Tap the mic and talk; the words show as you say them. T opens the text field, + attaches a picture or a file, and pictures can wait above the field while you type.

entries.title: Your agents top left, the record top right
entries.what: Top left, the menu with settings, then the agent you are talking to: tap the name to switch. Top right, the chat record. Nothing else sits on the stage.

entries.title: The stage moves with the agent
entries.what: Looking, making, found it, the answer and the questions each move in the agent's own way. Coach is snappy, Wizard is heavy and punchy. Say how an agent should move, in a few words, and it keeps that look. Reduce Motion holds it still.

entries.title: A live picture behind the words
entries.what: The agent can put a moving picture behind the stage: aurora, orb, waves, grain or bloom, in its own colors. It is drawn on the phone's graphics chip and goes still on Low Power or Reduce Motion. Try every look in the playground.

entries.title: The picture listens
entries.what: The picture moves with your voice while you talk, with the agent's voice while it reads the answer, and with the music when a beat plays.

entries.title: Keys and chords that play
entries.what: Ask for keys and you get a keyboard with a scale lock, so nothing sounds wrong. Ask for chords and you get pads, one chord each. Both play on Yui's own sound engine, even with the ringer on silent.
entries.yl: keys Am pentatonic sound=pad +send

groups.title: The full screen stage, drawn first
groups.lede: The new face of Yui, drawn on the web first. You talk, the answer plays full screen in short parts with a picture each, the questions come last with one Send, and the chat is only the record. Chris approved the mock on Sep 26, and it reached phones in Yui 0.4.0. Shots come from the playground mock in light and dark.

entries.title: Stage first: live on the full screen
entries.what: Send your first message and the whole screen is the answer. It plays as short parts, a line and a drawing each, the questions come last with one Send, and the chat keeps the record, top right. Tap it: this phone is the mock Chris approved on Sep 26. It is in the app since Yui 0.4.0.

entries.title: A short answer, straight to the stage
entries.what: Ask if you are on the newest build and the stage opens right away: a working line while the agent looks, then one sentence and a picture. No three dots in a chat, no deck of pages to get through.

entries.title: Questions last, one Send
entries.what: When the agent needs something from you, it waits until the end and asks it all on one page. Pick your answers, tap Send once.

entries.title: The chat is the record
entries.what: The chat moves behind the button top right. Every part you saw sits there as one row, a small picture and its line, with your answers under them. You read it when you want to look back.

entries.title: The stage moves with the agent
entries.what: The same turn on two agents: Coach is snappy, Sage is calm. Listening, working, found it, the answer and the questions each move in the agent's own way, and Reduce Motion holds it still. Tap it to open the mock.

entries.title: Say how each agent moves
entries.what: Tell an agent how it should move, in a few words, and it saves a motion look: heavy and punchy, or drifts like water. The same turn on two agents, each moving the way it was described. Type your own words to try one. Tap it to open the mock.

entries.title: A big mic bottom right, your agents top left
entries.what: Tap the mic and talk. T opens the text field, + attaches a picture or a file. Top left: the menu with settings, then the agent you are talking to. Drawn in the mock first; in the app since Yui 0.4.0.

groups.title: Yui 0.3.2
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.3.2 (build 176, Sep 26): a looper and drum pads that play in the app, hold to reply, a quiet dot on the menu, and a working row that says what the agent is doing and how long it usually takes. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: A beat from any agent
entries.what: Ask any agent for a beat and it sends a step looper that plays in the app. Rows are sounds, columns are steps. Tap cells while it plays, change the tempo and swing, and Send hands your version back in the same words. Runs on Yui's own sound engine.
entries.yl: loop@beat 90 "Boom bap" steps=16 swing=25 rows=kick|snare|clap|hat|open|rim p=x......x..x.....|....x.......x...|............x...|x.x.x.x.x.x.x...|..............x.|...x.......x....

entries.title: Drum pads that record
entries.what: Big pads that hit the moment you touch them. Record counts you in, keeps two bars and sends the take back to the agent as a loop, in time with the looper.
entries.yl: drums 2x2 "Tap a beat" +record bpm=90

entries.title: Hold to reply
entries.what: Swipe to reply is gone. Hold a message and tap Reply; the reactions, Copy and Select text sit in the same menu. A sideways drag now always switches screens. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.
entries.change: Hold to reply, no more swipe

entries.title: A quiet dot on the menu
entries.what: The count on the menu button is gone. A small dot springs on while something waits on you and springs off when you answer the last one. VoiceOver still says how many. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.
entries.change: A quiet dot on the menu button

entries.title: It says what it is doing
entries.what: The working row shows what your agent is doing in a few plain words, with a thin bar when it knows the steps: Checking the weather, then Drafting the plan, then the answer. Each line replaces the last and the reply clears the row.

entries.title: How long it usually takes
entries.what: Under the working row, the phone says how long this agent's turns usually take, like an app install: Usually 1 to 2 min. Past that it says Longer than usual, and that you can leave. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.
entries.change: Working row says how long this agent usually takes

groups.title: Yui 0.3.1
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.3.1 (build 160, Sep 26): what you were typing stays put, a lesson is one deck, and an ask you answered leaves the war room at once. All three came from the feedback button. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: What you were typing stays put
entries.what: Each agent's thread keeps its own unsent words, saved as you type and cleared when you send. A full screen, another agent, leaving the app or closing it all leave them in the box. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.

entries.title: Line breaks read as lines
entries.what: Basil listed five dinners in one bubble with \n between them, and the app showed the letter n. Now the native runtime turns each break into its own line, and a run of bullets into a list.
entries.yl:
say "A few protein-forward dinners that skip your peanut and shellfish allergies:"
list "Grilled chicken with roasted sweet potato and greens" "Salmon with rice and steamed broccoli" "Turkey meatballs with whole-wheat pasta and marinara" "Tofu or chickpea curry with coconut milk and rice"
say "Any of those sound good?"
choose "Pick a direction" "Chicken & sweet potato"|"Salmon & rice"|"Turkey meatballs"|"Tofu curry"

entries.title: Where is a map
entries.what: Ask where, about a place, a past empire, a trip or a delivery area, and the answer leads with a map: the land filled in, pins on the places, routes that trace themselves on. Chris asked about the Mongols and got a number and four compass points; now every page is a map.

entries.title: A map, not compass points
entries.what: The same question before and after channel guide v37: on the left the real answer from build 208, a big number and East, West, South, North in words. On the right the answer an agent sends now.

entries.title: Explainers draw every page
entries.what: Ask how a place, a past or a thing works and every page of the answer is a picture: a rough map drawn in shapes, a chart, a big number. Chris asked for a brief geography of the Mongols and got a page of text; now agents draw it.

entries.title: A map, not a text bomb
entries.what: The same question before and after the new rule in the channel guide: a paragraph and bullets, then a map and a chart.

entries.title: Flows never dead-end
entries.what: Ask Yui to interview you and the questions land on screen. No app build runs flows yet, so Yui sends the flow as a plan: the same questions, one at a time, one submit. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.

entries.title: Questions, not a headline
entries.what: The same answer before and after: a headline over a flow the phone could not run, then the intake questions with one submit.

entries.title: A lesson is one deck
entries.what: A deck page can hold a diagram, a formula, a chart, a big number or a calculator as its picture. So a lesson is one deck you swipe: an idea per page, a quiz, and the sliders on the last page. Older phones get the same pieces on one full screen.

entries.title: An answered ask leaves
entries.what: Tap an answer on an ask in the war room and the war room redraws right away, without it. The war room itself is down to four parts: one status line, at most three asks, Now and next, and one link to the board. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.
entries.change: An answered war room ask leaves at once

groups.title: Build 155
groups.lede: What build 155 (Sep 26) added to phones: talk to your agents hands-free and read the answers, a full screen that puts the keyboard away, plan questions in the middle of the page, and a Yui that holds less in memory. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account; the memory numbers are drawn live from the release test.

entries.title: Talk hands-free, read the answer
entries.what: Tap the mic once and Yui keeps listening between turns. Your words show as you say them, a short pause sends them, the answer comes back as text, and the mic opens again once it lands. The bar says where you are: Listening, on it, Your turn or Paused. One button stops it, and holding the mic still works the old way.

entries.title: A full screen puts the keyboard away
entries.what: Open anything full screen, a timer, a deck, a plan or a picture, and the keyboard goes down as it opens. Close it and the keyboard stays down, with what you typed still in the box. Before and after, from Chris's TestFlight feedback.
entries.change: A full screen takes the keyboard down with it

entries.title: A plan's question sits in the middle
entries.what: A short plan step, like a slider question, sits centered between the progress bar and Back and Next, with no card of its own: the page is the card. Long steps still start at the top and scroll.
entries.change: A plan's question sits in the middle of the screen

entries.title: Yui holds less in memory
entries.what: One scripted session on the simulator: five agents with 486-message threads, galleries, decks, games and full screens. Peak memory fell from 243 MB to 203 MB and launch from 137 MB to 124 MB, and the session ends with no new leaks, down from about 1,550 leaked objects. The same session runs before every release now and fails on a new leak or a peak over 300 MB.
entries.yl:
say "Memory in one long session, before and after build 155."
stat 203MB "Peak memory" delta=-40 good=down sub="was 243 MB"
stat 124MB "At launch" delta=-13 good=down sub="was 137 MB"
stat 0 "New leaks" delta=-1550 good=down sub="was about 1,550 objects"
chart bar "Memory in MB" x=Launch|Peak y=137|243 y2=124|203 names=Before|After unit=MB

groups.title: Build 148
groups.lede: What build 148 (Sep 26) added to Yui 0.3.0: your agent's settings in its drawer, a way to change one by talking about it, and timeline rows that move without resending the page. Send and the drawer got faster too, under Taps answer at once. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: Agent controls in the drawer
entries.what: The drawer's Controls tab talks to the Mac your agent runs on. Read and edit its personality, forget one memory, switch a skill off, pause a schedule or run it now. A change lands in about a second with no chat turn, every delete asks first, and a line with a key in it never leaves the Mac.

entries.title: Talk about a setting
entries.what: Tap Talk about this on any setting in Controls and it rides above the composer. Say what you want; your agent proposes a before and after, and one tap applies it on your Mac. Keys never leave the Mac.

entries.title: A timeline row moves in place
entries.what: One short line from the agent turns a running row done where it stands, and the Now line moves past it. No resent page, no jump, no buzz. A timeline opened alone full screen keeps its rows tight and starts at the top. Press Send on the agent line in the playground to watch a row move.

groups.title: Yui 0.3.0
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.3.0 (build 138, Sep 26), the smooth release: taps that answer at once, typing that keeps up, shapes that move, and a new look for Yui just by asking. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: Taps answer at once
entries.what: A long thread opens in about a third of a second instead of three, taps answer in under a tenth of a second, and scrolling a 500-message thread barely drops a frame. Same look, just fast. Build 148 made send and the menu drawer faster too: the drawer opens in about 66 ms, down from up to 172.

entries.title: Typing keeps up
entries.what: Hold backspace or tap space twice for a period and it keeps up like Notes, even on a long thread. A key only redraws the box you type in now.

entries.title: Shapes that move
entries.what: An agent explains how something works with a small drawing: circles, boxes, blobs and arrows that come on one after another, with a caption. Drawn on the phone, in the agent's colors.

entries.title: Restyle Yui by asking
entries.what: Ask any of your agents to make Yui feel like autumn. You see the new look beside yours, light and dark, and nothing changes until you tap to use it. Undo and Back to Yui's look are always there.

groups.title: Yui 0.2.0
groups.lede: What reached phones with Yui 0.2.0 (build 122, Sep 25): a home for every agent, screens that change in place, drawings, and a Settings line that says which Yui you have. Shots are real captures from the iPhone simulator on the demo account.

entries.title: Each agent gets a drawer
entries.what: Drag right on the chat and the agent's home follows your finger: pinned screens, what is waiting on you, controls and about. Your other agents spring up from the bottom.

entries.title: Agents fill the drawer
entries.what: One new word, menu, lets an agent put things in its drawer: a question in Review, a plan in Backlog, a shortcut you tap to start. The drawer is drawn by the app; the phone here shows the reply.
entries.yl:
say "Added to my drawer: one question, two plans, a shortcut."
menu review@dana "Invite Dana to the beta?" sub="asked yesterday"
menu backlog@trip "Meal plan for the trip" sub=queued
menu backlog@deload "Deload week plan" sub=drafting
menu shortcut@log "Log a meal" say="Log a meal: "

entries.title: Screens update in place
entries.what: Give a row a name and a later reply changes just that row. A timer, a score or a status line updates where it sits instead of arriving again, and a reply that only changes the screen doesn't buzz your phone.
entries.yl:
say "Leg day, live. A later reply changes one row by its name."
timeline "Leg day"
done@warmup "Warm-up" sub="10 min"
now@squat "Back squat" sub="set 2 of 4"
next@lunge "Walking lunges"

entries.title: The app draws
entries.what: An agent can draw instead of explain: a window, a phone or a chat bubble, with rows struck out, highlighted or greyed and a short note beside each.

entries.title: One Update chip, not red lines
entries.what: When an agent sends something your copy of Yui can't draw yet, the reply shows what it can and one small Update Yui to see this chip, never a row of errors.

entries.title: Settings says which Yui you have
entries.what: The bottom of Settings names the Yui on your phone: version and build, where it came from, the commit and build date, and the channel guide your agents read. Tap it to copy the lot into feedback.

groups.title: Music
groups.lede: Yui for musicians. Each instrument is one line from the agent, and plays in your browser now. The app gets them step by step on one sound engine.

entries.title: Tune up, keep time, send a take
entries.what: A guitarist before practice: tune up on the mic, a click at 90, a beat under it, Record, then Stop and send gives the agent the sound and the notes. A MIDI keyboard plays the keys. Turn your sound on.

entries.title: Music tools
entries.what: Six instruments an agent sends in one line each: a step looper, drum pads, an easy keyboard, chord buttons, a tuner and a metronome. They play for real in your browser with Web Audio; turn your sound on. In the app they share one sound engine: the looper and drum pads since Yui 0.3.2, keys and chords since 0.4.0, and the tuner and metronome since 0.4.1, with Record on every instrument and a MIDI keyboard.
entries.yl:
say "Six instruments, one line each. Here is the whole drum kit; the playground has all six."
drums 4x4 "The whole kit"

entries.title: loop
entries.what: A step looper. Rows are sounds, columns are steps. The agent writes a beat, you tap cells while it plays, and Send hands your version back in the same words.
entries.yl: loop@beat 90 "Boom bap" steps=16 swing=25 rows=kick|snare|clap|hat|open|rim p=x......x..x.....|....x.......x...|............x...|x.x.x.x.x.x.x...|..............x.|...x.......x....

entries.title: drums
entries.what: Big pads that play the moment you touch them, 2x2 or 4x4. Record counts you in, keeps two bars and sends the take back as a loop.
entries.yl: drums 2x2 "Tap a beat" +record bpm=90

entries.title: keys
entries.what: An easy keyboard with a scale lock: keys outside the scale are dimmed, so nothing sounds wrong. Pick a sound above it.
entries.yl: keys Am pentatonic sound=pad +send

entries.title: chords
entries.what: One big button per chord, from a key and a progression like I-V-vi-IV. A tap strums it. One patch moves every chord to a new key.
entries.yl: chords G I-V-vi-IV +send

entries.title: tuner
entries.what: Guitar, ukulele, bass or any note, on the mic. A needle shows how many cents off you are and turns green when you are close. Tap a string to hear its note.
entries.yl: tuner guitar

entries.title: metronome
entries.what: A big tempo, tap tempo and a dot per beat. It sits in the chat, and tells the agent how long you practiced.
entries.yl: metronome 90

entries.title: Record a take
entries.what: Record on the looper, the pads, the keys or the chords records what Yui plays, not the mic. Stop and send gives the agent the sound as an .m4a and the notes as a .mid, like a photo you took.
entries.yl: loop 120 "Take one" p=x...x...|..x...x.|xxxxxxxx +play

entries.title: A MIDI keyboard plays the keys
entries.what: Plug in a USB keyboard or pair one over Bluetooth, and it plays the keys on screen: each note lights up and counts as played. While a beat plays, Yui sends MIDI clock so your drum machine keeps time.
entries.yl: keys C major +send

groups.title: Questions and answers
groups.lede: The first screens an agent learned. Each is one line of text from the agent; each tap goes back to it as an event.

entries.title: ask
entries.what: A yes or no question with big buttons.

entries.title: choose
entries.what: One answer from a few, with a type-your-own escape hatch.
entries.yl: choose "Which split today?" Push|Pull|Legs +other

entries.title: pick
entries.what: Several answers at once, with a cap and a Done button.
entries.yl: pick "What gear do you have?" Dumbbells|Bench|Bands|"Pull-up bar"|Kettlebell +other max=3

entries.title: slide
entries.what: A number on a scale, with words at each end.
entries.yl: slide "Energy today" 1-5 "Wiped"|"Fired up"

entries.title: form
entries.what: A few fields in one card: text, sliders, switches, choices.
entries.yl: form "Daily check-in" mood:1-5 "Trained today":yes split:Push|Pull|Legs submit="Log it"

entries.title: list
entries.what: A checklist the person ticks off as they go.
entries.yl: list Today "Back squat 5x5 @ 225" "Bench 5x5 @ 185" "Barbell row 3x10" "Plank 3x60s" +check

entries.title: timer
entries.what: Intervals, rounds and rest. A workout timer opens full screen.

entries.title: card
entries.what: A picture, a title, a line of detail and one button.
entries.yl: card "Leg day" "Squat, RDL, walking lunges. About 45 minutes." sub="Thursday" img=/yl/legday.svg cta="Start workout"

entries.title: table
entries.what: Rows and columns, sortable, with units.

entries.title: camera
entries.what: Asks for a photo. The picture goes to the agent.
entries.yl: camera "Snap your plate"

entries.title: mic
entries.what: Asks for a voice note. Drawn on the web today; the app gets it with voice (YUI-14).
entries.yl: mic "What did you eat today?"

groups.title: Pictures and video
groups.lede: For anyone who works with images: pick the best shots, compare an edit, review a cut, plan a reel.

entries.title: Snap your plate, the model that sees reads it
entries.what: Native agents pick a model per turn: GLM 5.2 for words, GLM-5V-Turbo when you send a photo, both on OpenRouter with data collection off. This is Basil's answer to a real pizza photo, from a live run. Native agents reach phones with the next release.
entries.yl:
table Margherita Part|Protein|Carbs|Fat|Cal "Crust|4|30|2|150" "Sauce|1|5|0|25" "Cheese|7|1|9|110" "Per slice|12|36|11|285" units=|g|g|g|kcal
choose "How many slices?" 1|2|3|4 +other

entries.title: image
entries.what: One picture. With +edit, the person circles what to change.

entries.title: gallery
entries.what: A grid, row, feed or coverflow of photos. Tap to open, or pick favorites.

entries.title: video
entries.what: A clip to watch, loop or approve.

entries.title: compare
entries.what: Before and after: a slider, side by side, or tap to flip, with the changes marked.

entries.title: storyboard
entries.what: Frames of a video or post, in order. Drag to reorder, comment on any one.

groups.title: Numbers, charts and science
groups.lede: For tracking progress and for learning: charts drawn from data, big numbers, equations, and calculators you can drag.

entries.title: stat
entries.what: A big number with its change and a sparkline.

entries.title: chart
entries.what: Line, bar, area, scatter, pie and donut, from numbers in the line or a live table.
entries.yl:
say "Down 2.3 pounds this week, right on plan."
stat 178.9lb Weight delta=-2.3 spark=181.2|180.6|179.8|178.9 good=down sub="this week"
chart line "Weight" x=Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu y=180|179|178.5|178.9 y2=180|179.5|179|178.5 names=Actual|Plan unit=lb

entries.title: math
entries.what: Typeset equations, from one line of TeX.

entries.title: step
entries.what: A derivation or a protocol, one step at a time, with timers where needed.

entries.title: calc
entries.what: A formula with sliders. Drag a value and the answer and chart follow.
entries.yl: calc "How far does it fly?" f="R = v^2*sin(2*a)/g" v=5-40@20m/s a=0-90@30deg g=9.81m/s^2 plot=a unit=m

entries.title: Agent tables: a workout log
entries.what: The agent keeps your sets on the phone and draws them: squat over time, best set per lift. Send a put and every view redraws.

entries.title: Agent tables: macros
entries.what: Meals logged by day: calories today as one number, today's plate as a table, protein by day as a chart.

entries.title: Agent tables: a simple CRM
entries.what: Deals with a stage, a value and a next date. Tick one won in the list and the phone writes it and tells the agent.

entries.title: Build my workout
entries.what: The coach keeps your moves and their swaps in tables. Today's session is rows you tick off, and a swap is one put: goblet squat becomes front squat, the sets stay. Try it here, the phone gets it next.

entries.title: Meal photo to macros
entries.what: Snap your plate and say what's in it. Basil answers at once, works out calories, protein, carbs and fat behind the scenes, then posts one breakdown with today's totals and keeps each food in your food memory. Nothing to weigh. Try the step-by-step version in the playground with a sample photo.

groups.title: Lessons and plans
groups.lede: Screens that hold other screens: a deck of pages, a plan that asks one thing at a time, a walkthrough read aloud.

entries.title: deck
entries.what: Pages to swipe through, with a quiz at the end.

entries.title: plan
entries.what: Plan mode: one question at a time, ending in a project card that reopens it.

entries.title: plan with pages
entries.what: Findings to read, then questions, full screen with one Send. The answers land in the chat as your own message.

entries.title: plan ends in Send
entries.what: The last button of a plan says Send, and a card with nothing to act on has no button at all. No Got it, no OK: every button does something.
entries.yl:
say "Two quick ones, then I send the brief to the studio."
plan@brief "Site brief"
pick@pages "Which pages?" Home|About|Classes|Contact
ask@launch "Launch before the holidays?" "Yes, Dec 1"|"No rush"

entries.title: flow
entries.what: A saved series of screens written in Mermaid, with branches: the answer to one question picks the next ones. Back walks the path you took, the review lists only what you answered on it, and one event goes back at the end.

entries.title: My flows
entries.what: Every saved flow in one list: the starters every Yui has, with the variants an agent made nested under the flow they came from, each with its step count. Tap a row to run it and see the path it took. Hold one of yours to remove it: a variant goes alone, a base asks first because its variants go with it, and a starter stays. Matches the app on main, in the next build.

entries.title: Meet Yui
entries.what: The first run as a flow: your name, how much you know about AI, what you want help with. Each answer changes the next screen, and it ends with two starter agents picked for you and how to connect them.

entries.title: A starter agent
entries.what: No agent yet? Pick Coach, Basil, Penny or Quill and it answers right away with a real question on a screen. Here a stand-in answers; in Yui it will be a model on Yui's hosted connector, planned and priced in the spec.

entries.title: Connect your tools
entries.what: Pick Google Calendar, Gmail or HubSpot, read what each one allows in plain words, and allow or skip each. Then the agent answers with one Sign in button per tool you allowed. Here the buttons open the spec: nothing signs in yet.

entries.title: narrate
entries.what: A walkthrough the agent reads aloud, frame by frame.

entries.title: timeline
entries.what: What shipped, what is running, what is next: done rows, a Now line, then the queue. Older rows fold; a row with a link opens Safari.

entries.title: sketch
entries.what: A small drawn picture: a window, phone or chat bubble with rows struck out, highlighted or called out with an arrow, and an optional before and after. Shows a change instead of describing it.

entries.title: shapes
entries.what: A small diagram that moves: circles, boxes, blobs, labels and arrows that come on one after another, with a caption under it. Explains how something works in a few lines, drawn on the phone instead of generated.

entries.title: Drag the queue into your own order
entries.what: Tap Edit order on a timeline and each queued row gets a drag handle; done and running rows stay put. Save sends the new order once. In the war room it lands straight on the board's priority, with no agent turn in between, and only the person who owns the agent can do it.

entries.title: The war room
entries.what: One screen to run a project from: what needs you (tap an answer and it lands on the card), what is running in each lane, the timeline, the newest builds with an Install button, the latest feedback and the card it became, and the MVP bar.

groups.title: Games
groups.lede: One line puts a small game on the phone, full screen. Tic-tac-toe is played against the agent, one move per turn; snake and memory run on the phone and send the score back.

entries.title: tic-tac-toe
entries.what: You tap a cell, the agent answers with its move. The phone calls the winner and offers Play again.

entries.title: snake
entries.what: Swipe or use the arrow pad. At game over the score goes back to the agent, which can set a best to beat.

entries.title: memory
entries.what: Match the pairs. The agent picks the faces: fruit, or the words you are learning.

groups.title: The app around the screens
groups.lede: Everything here is a real capture from the iPhone simulator.

entries.title: Every agent keeps its own tables
entries.what: Each agent has a small database of its own, filled with good starter values: Yui's groceries and to-dos, Basil's foods and meals, Arnold's exercises and sessions. Ask it to add, log or total something and it answers with the table. A delete always asks first.
entries.yl:
list title="Still to get" "Bread · 1 loaf · Bakery" "Eggs · 1 dozen · Dairy" "Milk · 1 gallon · Dairy" "Coffee · 1 bag · Pantry" "Bananas · 6 · Produce"
choose "Delete Coffee from groceries?" Delete|Keep

entries.title: Every agent says what it does
entries.what: Each starter carries a line under its name, two sentences on what it does and three things to ask it, so you know before you open it. A hello is an answer on the stage: Gouda's first beat and pick play in the chat and never wait in Review.
entries.yl: table Crew Agent|"What it does" "Yui|Ask anything, or make a new agent" "Arnold|Workouts built around your week and body" "Basil|Eat better without counting everything" "Gouda|Beats, chords and practice, right on screen" "Penny|Get your week out of your head" "Quill|Learn anything fast, then get quizzed"

entries.title: What can you do for me?
entries.what: Ask a starter agent what it does and it answers in one line, then a list and buttons to start, never markdown bullets cut into pages. This is Basil's real answer on the live runtime; the shots are before and after in the app.
entries.yl:
list title="What I do" "Meal plans around your goal" "Macros from a photo of your plate" "Grocery lists you can check off" "Smart swaps for cravings" "Check-ins to stay on track"
choose "Where to start?" "Plan my meals"|"Read my plate"|"Build a grocery list"|"Just answer a question" +other

entries.title: The starter crew says hello
entries.what: Every new person starts with six agents, each with its own look and its own first screen: Yui asks where to start, Arnold and Basil ask about your health before any plan, Gouda puts a beat on, Penny opens a form for the week and Quill asks what to learn. A live check asks each of them two things and scores every answer.
entries.yl: choose "Where do you want to start?" "Get fit"|"Eat better"|"Make music"|"Plan my week"|"Learn something" +other

entries.title: One Send per screen, picks too
entries.what: A pick inside a plan is just its options. Every tap rides the screen's one Send, and the review lists what you picked.

entries.title: One Send per screen, forms too
entries.what: A form inside a plan is just fields. The questions screen keeps one Send, and your name, role and one-liner ride in the plan's answer. From Chris's TestFlight feedback.

entries.title: First run
entries.what: From sign-in to Yui talking on the whole screen: your crew is already in your list, nothing to pair. Take them all out and the first screen offers them back, one tap each or Add all 6, or you connect your own agent.

entries.title: Connect your agent
entries.what: Your own agent: three commands on your computer and a pairing code. Your agent dials out; your machine opens no ports. Say hi and it answers on the whole screen.

entries.title: Your agent answers with screens
entries.what: Each agent gets a thread and a short guide that teaches it every screen above. Ask, and the answer plays on the stage, full screen: the words big, then the list and the timer as real screens, the question last. The chat, top right, keeps the record of every turn.

entries.title: Your agents, your list
entries.what: Add, rename and remove agents yourself. The name top left opens the list, each agent with a line on what it does; Manage agents has the rest.

entries.title: A look for every agent
entries.what: Coral wordmark, letter avatars, light and dark, and a look per agent: the whole stage takes its color, and the agent can change it with one line.

entries.title: Full screen when it matters
entries.what: Answers play on the whole phone, and a workout keeps going. Open the chat, top right, and a pill keeps the timer running there; tap it and the timer is back on the stage.

entries.title: The shelf
entries.what: An agent saves a screen by name and it lands on the shelf at the top of the chat. Tap it to reopen it full screen, no message needed; the agent brings it back with two tokens (show busy day).

entries.title: Timer on the lock screen
entries.what: A running timer keeps counting on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, in the agent's look. Pause, resume or end it without opening the app.

entries.title: Change your answer
entries.what: The questions come last, on one screen with one Send. Tap again to change a choice before you send, or later in the chat; the agent hears changed: true. It can lock one on purpose with +lock.

entries.title: Pictures in, photos out
entries.what: Agents send pictures and videos they make, and they play on the stage. You send photos with the + button.

entries.title: A buzz when your agent answers
entries.what: A push when the app is closed, none while you are watching the thread, and a mute switch per agent.

entries.title: Pick it up in Yui
entries.what: From Telegram, "send it to Yui" drops the screen into that agent's thread and pushes it to your phone.

entries.title: React to a message
entries.what: In the chat, hold a message from your agent and pick one of six. Each is an instruction: 👍 build it, 👎 no, 🤔 ask me, ❤️ keep it, ⏳ later, 🔥 do it next.

entries.title: Type / for your agent's commands
entries.what: Tap T in the chat and type a slash: Yui lists the commands your agent already takes, each with one line on what it does. Keep typing to narrow it, tap one to fill it in, and Send hands it to the agent as is. The list comes from the agent's own computer, so a new skill shows up on its own. Agents that have no commands show nothing.

entries.title: @ another agent
entries.what: Tap T in the chat and type @: your other agents come up with their faces and whether they are online. Tap one and the bar says who it goes to. Send, and it answers from its own thread; its answer shows up in this one too, in its own colors, with a way into its thread. An agent that is asleep or offline says so in one line.

entries.title: Restyle Yui by asking
entries.what: Ask any of your agents to make Yui feel like autumn. A card shows the new look beside the one you have, light or dark, and nothing changes until you tap Use autumn. Then Undo puts it back, and Settings > Look always has Back to Yui's look. Your agents keep their own looks in their threads unless you turn that off. Text stays readable and buttons stay the same size, whatever the look. In the app since Yui 0.3.0; try it in the playground too.

entries.title: Invite someone, their agents are waiting
entries.what: Pick which of your agents a person gets, the look for each and what each says first, then tap Invite. When they sign in, their list is already filled, a new message waiting from each agent. Only agents that pass the safe-to-share rules can be picked, and taking one back removes it from their app at once. In the app now: a shared agent waits in the person's list in its look, with its first message, its settings say Shared by, and yours say whether an agent is safe to share. Try both sides in the playground.

entries.title: Group threads
entries.what: Several of your agents in one conversation. The one you @ answers, and the lead answers the rest. When one agent asks another, a row shows who asked whom. A budget stops them handing work around forever: past it, you see the held ask and choose Let it or Stop here. Try it in the playground. The database and agent side reached phones with Yui 0.3.0; the app's own screens come in a later release.

entries.title: Reply to a message
entries.what: In the chat, hold a message and tap Reply. The quote sits above your words, your agent gets it with your answer, and tapping the quote on your reply scrolls back to the original.

entries.title: A reply quotes the whole screen
entries.what: Reply to a card and the bar above your words now shows its title and the first lines under it, not the title alone. Your agent gets the same lines with your answer, so it knows which screen you mean.

entries.title: Copy any part of a message
entries.what: Hold a message in the chat and tap Select text. Its words open on their own page, read only: drag to pick the part you want and Copy, or Copy all. A message at the bottom of the screen lifts so the menu never covers it.
entries.change: Copy any part of a message

entries.title: Links open Safari
entries.what: A card with a link gets an arrow on its button. Tap it and the page opens in Safari, and nothing goes to the chat, so the agent never answers a tap that already did its job. Buttons without a link still answer the agent.
entries.yl:
card "A new test build" body="Links open Safari, Select text, the war room timeline" cta=Install url=https://www.yuigui.com/install.html
choose "Anything else?" "What changed?"|"Not now"

entries.title: Jump to the newest message
entries.what: The stage always shows the newest turn. In the chat, scrolled up a long thread, a round arrow above the mic counts the agent's new messages and takes you back down in one tap.

entries.title: Hold to talk
entries.what: Hold the big mic, bottom right, and talk. Your words show on the stage as you say them, and the mic beats with your voice. Let go and they go to your agent; slide left to the trash to cancel. A tap instead of a hold talks hands-free, and the listening runs on the phone. Holding works on the camera too: Hold to snap and say.

entries.title: Screens beside the chat
entries.what: The stage has pages beside the answer, a swipe away, each there once the agent puts something on it. An agent leaves your week on one and your notes on another while you keep talking. In the chat, a chip under the answer says On screen 2 and takes you there.
entries.yl:
>2 timer 25m Focus
>3 list@shop Shopping Eggs|Spinach|Rice|Gochujang +check
choose "Protein?" Beef|Tofu|"Just the egg"

entries.title: Chat with a screen
entries.what: An agent opens a screen to chat with one word, talk. Tap T there and type: it reaches the agent tagged with that screen, and your message shows in the chat marked From screen 2.
entries.yl:
>2 list@runs Runs "Tue 5k"|"Thu 5k"|"Sat 10k" +check
>2 talk
say Your week is on screen 2. Type changes there.

entries.title: Nothing gets lost
entries.what: Messages wait for a sleeping Mac or a dropped network, with a clear mark when they land. History is kept 90 days, with limits that keep the service safe for strangers.

entries.title: Sign in, try the demo, get help
entries.what: Sign in with Apple, delete your account in the app, a demo code for reviewers, and help one tap away.

entries.title: One working row
entries.what: While your agent works, the stage shows its mark breathing and one line under it: On its way until it picks your message up, then a working word and the time, like Figuring it out · 7s. The word changes every few seconds. The chat shows the same line in one row, and it goes when the answer lands.

entries.title: It says what it is doing
entries.what: While your agent works, the stage says what it is doing in a few plain words, with a thin bar when it knows the steps: Reading your calendar, then Checking the weather, then the answer. The working row in the chat says the same. The seconds keep counting, and the reply clears it. No bubble, no push.
entries.change: Pondering becomes what it is doing

entries.title: Not listening yet
entries.what: An agent that is paired but whose gateway has not started says so, instead of reading online. Its sheet shows the one command left to run, and a message you send it waits, then gets answered once the gateway is up.

entries.title: Any A2A agent
entries.what: Agents built with ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI or Microsoft Agent Framework join by their Agent Card. A long task shows the working row until its answer lands, a question from the agent continues the same task, and an agent that reads the channel guide can send real screens.

entries.title: Your own model
entries.what: A model you run yourself with Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM joins through the model bridge. Yui sends it the channel guide and the thread every turn, so even a small local model draws screens and remembers your taps.

entries.title: Yui screens in Telegram
entries.what: When the app is not around, the same screen reaches you in Telegram. Questions are buttons under the message and a tap answers your agent. A timer, a chart or a form opens in a Telegram Mini App, in the chat's own colors.

entries.title: Long messages read as pages
entries.what: A long agent message never fills the chat. It folds to its first lines and a Read as pages button, which opens it as pages you swipe through, one idea per page.

entries.title: Full-screen pages tell a story
entries.what: Full screen is the whole stage, with no card on it. One idea per page, the headline set big and sized to its words, the body in a quieter voice, and words that spring on and off with the page. In the chat, the same deck waits folded until you open it.

entries.title: Your workout runs on its own clock
entries.what: Tap Start and the session runs itself: a work set, the rest countdown with what is next, the next set, the next move. Arnold gives one line per move. Heavy lifters get a to-failure last set with a big Stop that logs the reps.

groups.title: On yuigui.com
groups.lede: The screen language, shown where people land, and the whole build history played back day by day.

entries.title: The site chat plays a whole flow
entries.what: Open the chat on any page and say show me a flow. Yui plays the first run of the app on the stage, one screen at a time with a branch on your answers, then one Send, and answers what you told it. This is the flow it runs.
entries.yl: flow@onboard onboarding

entries.title: The library
entries.what: Every screen an agent can send, live, with its line, and every saved flow drawn as its Mermaid chart. Search it, copy a line, or open one in the playground. Agents read the same list at /library.json and search it by intent at /api/library or with the yui_library MCP tool.

entries.title: Five lines, five screens
entries.what: The quick start at the top of /yl. Tap a line to draw it; the app draws the same line the same way.
entries.yl: choose "What are we training?" Push|Pull|Legs +other

entries.title: Watch Yui grow
entries.what: The Timeline page replays every shipped change that has a screenshot, oldest first, while the commit and build counters climb. Drag the slider to jump to any day.

entries.title: The three lines challenge
entries.what: Anyone can add a screen of three lines or fewer to the community gallery with a pull request. Every entry is drawn live and opens in the playground.
entries.yl:

choose "Your vote?" Tacos|Ramen|Pizza +other
table Votes Dish|Votes "Tacos|2" "Ramen|1" "Pizza|0"

entries.title: Share any screen
entries.what: Every screen here has its own link with a preview that shows the lines and the screen they draw. Share in the playground puts your lines in the link, and one iframe puts a live screen on your own page.
entries.yl:

entries.title: Ask for a hand
entries.what: The public TestFlight beta is open to anyone. This form is the other way in: for people with no agent yet, who want help connecting one, or who want the invite by email. Your name, the email on your Apple ID and a phone number; Apple emails the TestFlight invite.

entries.title: Yui screens inside Claude
entries.what: The same Yui Lines draw right in the chat of apps that support MCP Apps, and on your phone. A tap in either place sends the same answer to the agent.
entries.yl:
say "Asked from the chat, answered in the chat or on your phone."
choose "Lunch?" Salad|Soup|Tacos

entries.title: Yui's values
entries.what: Eight values on one page, the test every screen has to pass: screens, not text bombs; one idea per page; type tells the story; draw it, don't describe it.

entries.title: The site reads like the app
entries.what: One type scale runs every page, the same one the app uses: big clear titles, short bodies, nothing cut off. Before and after, on a phone and a wide screen.

groups.title: Planned, not built
groups.lede: What these cards will look like, drawn by the web renderer from Yui Lines that parse today. None of it is in the app yet, except where an entry says so.

entries.title: Agents that live in Yui
entries.what: Yui's own engine is built and tested: one runtime runs every person's native agents, no Hermes and no pairing. On a local test, Gouda answered 'make me a lo-fi beat' with this playing loop. It is switched off until the new backend and the model key go live, then it ships with the native sprint build.

entries.title: Yui says hello first
entries.what: Yui's first answer, straight from her profile folder, with no model and no setup: hi, who is on your crew, and a real question on a screen. Every native agent is a folder of three files: who it is, the screens it reaches for first, and its first answer. The build checks every folder and stops on one that breaks the rules. Switched off until the native sprint build.
entries.yl: choose "Where do you want to start?" "Get fit"|"Eat better"|"Make music"|"Plan my week"|"Learn something" +other

entries.title: Voice in, text out
entries.what: Talk, read the answer, hands free and fast. Hold to talk and hands-free voice are in the app now (build 155 on, on-device listening). Still to come: the answer streaming in word by word.
entries.yl: mic "What did you eat today?"

entries.title: Where the next release stands
entries.what: The top of the war room: the cards in the next version, done, running or queued, then the ship steps (tests, one upload, VALID, what to try goes out), then everything on main since the last TestFlight build. Built from the board's own exports, never typed by an agent. On the site now; on the phone it will patch in place as cards move.

entries.title: Your tables on a second device
entries.what: Not in v1: tables stay on your iPhone and ride its backup. When a second Yui device arrives, sync is one switch in Settings, off by default, no new account. A second device joins by QR, every change is sealed on the phone, and Yui's server holds boxes it cannot open. Turning it off deletes the server's copy. Drawn in the playground; not in the app yet.

entries.title: Your keys, on your phone
entries.what: Your own fal, Replicate, OpenRouter, Anthropic or OpenAI key goes in once, in Settings > Keys, and stays in the iPhone's Keychain. An agent asks to use one, Yui draws the ask, and you allow, allow once or say no. The agent gets a handle, never the key, and spends inside a monthly cap you set. In the app since Yui 0.6.0, build 370; try it in the playground.

entries.title: The model on the phone
entries.what: Apple's on-device model does four small jobs: reply chips under a screen that asks in words, a pill that says which agent in a group your message is for, a real line on the lock screen, and a draft screen when there is no signal. It never answers as an agent and nothing leaves the phone. Drawn in the playground; not in the app yet.

entries.title: Widgets and Siri
entries.what: A saved screen pinned to the home screen or the lock screen: a stat with its trend, a checklist you tick on the widget, a timer you start without opening Yui. The agent keeps it current with the same patches it sends today, and every tap goes back to it. Siri asks an agent, shows a screen or starts a timer. Drawn in the playground; not in the app yet.

entries.title: The Speed panel
entries.what: How fast Yui is on real phones, in the war room: typing, messages landing, scrolling, hangs and memory, each with a trend per build, and a chart that steps down when a fix lands. The budget behind every number is written down. Sample numbers for now; the phone starts reporting with YUI-102.
